answer: Trust-graph random walks (SybilRank): honest agents form a dense web, while a sybil farm is an island joined to it by a few attack edges. Seeded verifiers spread trust in walks of log n steps; each walk is a ripple that rarely crosses those thin bridges, so island nodes end with near-zero trust. Theory bounds the payoff at about log n sybils per attack edge: in a 16,000-agent network, admitting 1,400 fakes needs 100 real vouches from honest peers. A gale of fake links inside the island buys nothing.
